_comment: Per-string context pushed to Crowdin by `npm run i18n:context`. One line per key saying where the string appears and what constrains it — the facts a translator cannot get from the English alone. Written when the string is, by whoever ran /wording. Keys mirror en.json.
back: Button returning from the account view to settings.
anonymous.name_label: Label beside the generated name of an anonymous account.
anonymous.state: One-line statement of what kind of admission the reader holds. Sits above the detail line.
anonymous.detail: Explains the consequence of the state above: this account lives on one device only. Two sentences at most.
anonymous.upgrade: Button turning an anonymous account into a permanent one. In-world word for registering.
anonymous.sign_out: Button. Destructive for an anonymous account — it opens the warning dialog below.
permanent.name_label: Label beside the reader's chosen name.
permanent.state: One-line statement of what kind of admission the reader holds.
permanent.detail: Explains the consequence: files follow them to any device.
permanent.sign_out: Button. Not destructive here — the account survives.
signed_out.state: One-line statement shown when nobody is signed in.
signed_out.detail: Explains what signing in would get them.
sign_out_warning.title: Title of the confirm dialog before an anonymous sign-out. States the stake plainly; this is the one irreversible action in the app.
sign_out_warning.message: Body of that dialog. Must make the loss unmistakable without scolding.
sign_out_warning.confirm: Confirm button naming both halves of what happens. Deliberately longer than the usual button budget — do not shorten it into a lie.
sign_out_warning.cancel: Cancel button, in-world: it names the thing being kept rather than saying Cancel. Must still be unmistakable as the safe choice.
